scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8129: A single Campus 1 workstation, PC11 on VLAN 20
(172.16.20.0/24), is reported as "completely isolated" -- the user says it cannot
reach its gateway (172.16.20.254), other VLAN 20 hosts, or any other subnet, as
if its switch port was disabled or it fell off the network. They want PC11's
isolation fixed. Please confirm the fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC11 (172.16.20.x on VLAN 20) reaches its
  gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0% loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and
  reaches off-subnet destinations across the core (OSPF converged). The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a single-host
  isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC11 isolated from
everything -- is NOT reproducible: PC11 reaches its gateway 172.16.20.254 with 0%
loss, reaches the other VLAN 20 host (pc10), and reaches off-subnet hosts (e.g. a
Campus 2 or other-VLAN address) across the converged core.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: PC11's connectivity is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces PC11's gateway,
intra-VLAN, and inter-subnet reachability, finds them working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a disabled port or an isolated host -- blaming the
switch port, the VLAN 20 SVI, or PC11's config to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket claims PC11 (172.16.20.11) on VLAN 20 is "completely
isolated," but direct evidence from the live lab shows the network is fully
healthy. PC11's eth0 is UP with the correct IP address (172.16.20.11/24) and
default gateway (172.16.20.254). Its switch port, switch2 eth5, is assigned to
the br_vlan20 bridge in forwarding state with no iptables, ebtables, or
traffic-control filters applied.

Connectivity tests from PC11 succeed across every relevant path: the VLAN 20
gateway (172.16.20.254) responds with 0% loss; both VLAN 20 peers PC9
(172.16.20.9) and PC10 (172.16.20.10) are reachable; inter-VLAN routing to
VLAN 10 (172.16.10.5) and VLAN 30 (172.16.30.12) works normally; and WAN-side
destinations (172.30.1.1, 172.25.1.1, 10.1.0.1) are also reachable via
multiple routing hops. The multilayer switch mswitch0, which holds the VLAN 20
SVI (172.16.20.254/24), has a complete OSPF routing table with a Full/DR
adjacency to router16 and routes to all subnets in the topology.

Root cause: there is no fault — the reported isolation does not exist in the
current lab state. The ticket describes a condition that is not present.

Corrective fix: no configuration change is required. The on-call engineer
should verify with the end user whether the symptom has self-resolved or was
misreported, and close the ticket as a false alarm.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup confirms PC11 reaches its gateway (172.16.20.254) with 0% loss, can reach same‑VLAN hosts (PC9/PC10), and reaches off‑subnet/WAN destinations, indicating a healthy baseline.

The agent reproduced key operational facts (PC11 interface up, gateway and multiple remote pings succeed, switch port in VLAN and no filtering) and correctly concluded no fault, though a couple of supervisory claims (e.g., a ‘complete OSPF routing table’) are not fully shown in the log and one ping attempt (172.16.5.1) returned unreachable but was not discussed. Overall the investigation supports the ‘no anomaly’ conclusion.
